alternatives.name: Podman / Quadlet
alternatives.why_not_default: Retained review establishes no native workload comparison. Filesystem/network enforcement, volume behavior, cleanup and host compatibility remain unmeasured. Rootless and systemd capabilities are documented in the [Quadlet reference](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html), but documentation does not qualify this workload.

alternatives.name: Docker Engine / Moby
alternatives.why_not_default: No retained matched execution establishes better isolation, reproduction or recovery for the selected tasks. [Rootless documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/rootless/) describes user-namespace operation and prerequisites; it supplies no local acceptance.

alternatives.name: Apple Container
alternatives.why_not_default: Native Mac execution retained a PostgreSQL row across stop/start and cleaned up owned resources. That storage check does not establish the required filesystem/network policy. The Documents bind mount stalled, and crash/reboot recovery remains unqualified.

alternatives.name: E2B
alternatives.why_not_default: The retained workflow is prospective: no sandbox was created or tested. Managed lifecycle and a separate VM boundary lack workload-specific enforcement, recovery and cleanup acceptance.

alternatives.name: gVisor
alternatives.why_not_default: Retained source review identifies an OCI application-kernel option, but no runsc workload/platform execution or matched isolation comparison establishes superiority for these bounded native tasks.

limits: This verdict reviews historical retained evidence; no native isolation or lifecycle trial was executed in this session.
The pinned Moby README could not be retrieved through either its GitHub URL or raw-content fallback. Its local retained review and Docker rootless documentation were readable.
Private raw artifacts behind sanitized receipts were not inspected.
Upstream documentation reads establish source-review context, not acceptance of the packet's current versions on this host.
open_gaps: Worktrees do not isolate permissions, accounts, global configuration or shared services; crash cleanup preserving dirty and unrelated state remains unproven.

Sandbox acceptance covers selected filesystem operations and Linux/WSL IPv4 loopback HTTP proxy policy. TLS, SOCKS, DNS rebinding, IPv6, remote hosts, resource limits and general escape resistance remain unqualified.
The HTTP fixture initially failed because proxy readiness raced client startup; acceptance used bounded connection-refused retries.
Overlapping read/write exclusions allowed an ephemeral write without changing the host; direct write denial was established only by the separate protected-write fixture.
Ordinary native clients and Dagu processes are not automatically wrapped in sandbox-runtime.
No retained matched comparison establishes that an OCI or managed VM alternative better satisfies this layer.
Historical Worktrunk lifecycle evidence does not independently establish identical behavior at the packet's newer pin.

arms: Worktrunk owned create/select/list/remove lifecycle, including preservation of dirty and unrelated state.
sandbox-runtime permitted/protected filesystem operations and allowed, explicit-deny and default-deny HTTP requests with independent server observation.
A task-required OCI or VM alternative executing equivalent boundary, workload, lifecycle and cleanup checks on the target host.
overturn_protocol.metric: Preserved edits and unrelated resources; permitted operations succeed; protected host paths remain unchanged; denied requests never reach the fixture server; required workload completes and owned resources clean up. Compare actual executions, not receipt replay or metadata.

overturn_when: Re-execute the Worktrunk and sandbox-runtime acceptance scopes recorded in blueprints/token-native-focus/saturation-audit.json on the required host and version. Change the affected selection if it loses dirty work, changes a protected host path, or delivers a denied request. Promote an alternative only after a matched execution passes those scopes and a concrete additional task requirement; for container persistence, include the native stop/start and cleanup check in blueprints/convergence-practice/container-storage/README.md. These paths define retained scopes and a storage recipe, not an already executed cross-runtime comparison.
why_selected: Select Worktrunk for separate editing state and activate sandbox-runtime only when the task requires enforced restrictions. docs/token-native-saturation.md and evidence/receipts/token-native-retained-functional-20260920.json record native Worktrunk create/select/list/remove in a disposable repository with hooks disabled; catalogs/foundation/decisions.json also records dirty-removal refusal without loss. evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json records native allowed writes, denied reads and separately denied protected writes. evidence/receipts/native-sandbox-network-20260920.json records native sandbox execution against a local HTTP fixture: the allowed request reached the server, while explicit-deny and default-deny requests did not. These are bounded native results using local fixtures, not a general security certification or a measured victory over container runtimes.
